newsitem.title: USA: Thomas & Betts looks to improve margins at Augat.
newsitem.headline: Thomas & Betts looks to improve margins at Augat.

text.p: Thomas & Betts Corp said on Monday that it can beef up operating margins in the electronics business with its purchase of Augat Inc, despite recent troubles in the industry, citing its track record in its own electronics business.

Thomas & Betts, which makes connectors and components for electrical and the electronics markets, said earlier that it agreed to buy Augat, which makes electric components for circuit connection, for $550 million in stock.
The move sparked questions for the Thomas & Betts, which has recently been focusing on its electrical business, which has higher margins and profits, analysts said.
One analyst on a conference call with Thomas & Betts officials asked why the company would make such an expensive foray back into electronics.
"Now you are going into (an area) more volatile, with greater price erosion and a record that has been more spotty ...This seems like a rather dramatic reversal of trends," the analyst said.

Thomas & Betts president Clyde Moore said the company's history of strength in the ailing industry meant the purchase was another opportunity for growth. He said Thomas & Betts improved operating margins in the electronics business from three percent in 1993 to seven percent in 1994 and then to 12.2 percent in 1995.
And in 1996, "a fairly difficult year, we improved it to the 14 percent range," Moore said. The figures are for North America and Asia and exclude Europe.
"We are on steady ground in this area. We looked for something similar and we found one," a company official said.
The company said its operating marging were at about 14 percent, while those of Augat were lower, although it did not disclose the exact amount.
